knowledge_point.title: Identifying the Horizontal Stretch and Vertical Shift of a Transformed Tangent Curve

question.:question/problem:
![](images/10/10912ded2166eb7ae28ee81c2936f008bf14eb288ec95969b822dd138be509d8.png)

The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(Bx)+D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $B+D?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The period $T$ of the function is

$$
T=\pi -(-\pi )=2\pi .
$$

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\operatorname{tan}⁡(Bx+C)+D$ is given by 

$$
T=\frac{\pi }{B}.
$$

Applying the formula of the period, we get

$$
2\pi =\frac{\pi }{B}\,⟹\,B=\frac{\pi }{2\pi }=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the tangent function. We see that the function has been translated by $1$ unit up. Hence, $D=1.$

Therefore, $B+D=\frac{1}{2}+1=\frac{3}{2}.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is

$$
y=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{2})+1.
$$

The graph above shows the function $y = \tan (Bx) + D$, where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $D - B$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The period $T$ of the function is

$$
T=\frac{3 \pi}{4}-(-\frac{3 \pi}{4})=\frac{3 \pi}{2}.
$$

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\tan(Bx+C)+D$ is given by 

$$
T=\frac{\pi}{B}.
$$

Applying the formula of the period, we get

$$
\frac{3 \pi}{2}=\frac{\pi}{B}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad B=\frac{\pi}{(\frac{3 \pi}{2})}=\frac{2}{3}.
$$

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the tangent function. We see that the function has been translated by $2$ units down. Hence, $D=-2.$

Therefore, $D-B=-2-(\frac{2}{3})=-\frac{8}{3}.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is

$$
y=\tan(\frac{2x}{3})-2.
$$

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the tangent function. We see that the function has been translated by $\frac{3}{4}$ units down. Hence, $D=-\frac{3}{4}.$

Therefore, $D-B=-\frac{3}{4}-(\frac{1}{3})=-\frac{13}{12}.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is

$$
y=\tan(\frac{x}{3})-\frac{3}{4}.
$$

The graph above shows the function $y=\tan(Bx)+D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $B+D?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The period $T$ of the function is

$$
T=\frac{2\pi }{3}-(-\frac{2\pi }{3})=\frac{4\pi }{3}.
$$

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\tan(Bx+C)+D$ is given by 

$$
T=\frac{\pi }{B}.
$$

Applying the formula of the period, we get

$$
\frac{4\pi }{3}=\frac{\pi }{B}\,⟹\,B=\frac{\pi }{(\frac{4\pi }{3})}=\frac{3}{4}.
$$

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the tangent function. We see that the function has been translated by $\frac{9}{4}$ units down. Hence, $D=-\frac{9}{4}.$

Therefore, $B+D=\frac{3}{4}+(-\frac{9}{4})=-\frac{3}{2}.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is

$$
y=\tan(\frac{3x}{4})-\frac{9}{4}.
$$
